summary: Fixed the journal fork-duplication bug by replacing session-keyed lookup with a project-wide entry-id lookup in journal-store, then wired the previously-unbuilt journal recorder into the agent runtime by adding a new memory-journal Pi extension with hooks for session_compact, session_before_tree, turn_end, and session_shutdown, and registering it via additionalExtensionPaths in pi-session-factory. Also added .gizmo/memory/journal/ to .gitignore. Typecheck clean, 155 tests pass (28 new), and the extension was verified to load via Pi's real resource loader.
decisions: Replace per-session resume key with a project-wide lastEntryId lookup (resumeAfter(entries)) so forked sessions, which preserve entry ids but change session id, resume where the parent left off instead of re-journaling inherited history.

Wire the journal recorder as a bundled Pi extension (apps/agent-server/src/pi-extensions/memory-journal.ts) loaded via additionalExtensionPaths rather than discovered, so memory journaling is on by default rather than per-project configuration.
Use session_before_tree hook to capture the branch being abandoned, which closes the abandoned-branch gap that getBranch() alone cannot (since it only returns the active path).
Truncate journal segments at session_compact up to firstKeptEntryId so the recorded span ends exactly where the model's context resumes.
Wrap every hook so a journaling failure logs but never touches the session, and gate everything on GIZMO_MEMORY_JOURNAL=0 to disable.
Add .gizmo/memory/journal/ to .gitignore with a comment explaining how to reverse it, chosen as the reversible default since .gizmo/ is tracked in this repo.

Accept a bounded duplicate-recording case: if a fork point falls inside an already-journaled segment, the entries from the fork point to that segment's end are recorded twice, traded off against the bloat of indexing every entry id per segment.
errors: Initial probe calling loadExtensionFactories() on the resource loader returned an empty list with no error, which would have falsely indicated the extension wasn't loading; the real load path is load() and its result lives in extensionsResult, which did show the memory-journal extension resolved and loaded cleanly.

Node ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED encountered when probing how the @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent package re-exports internal modules, resolved by loading via the package's public resource loader instead of reaching into dist internals.
